text:
Flying into Sapporo this winter? On 25 and 26 January 2026 heavy snow cancelled 1,145 JR Hokkaido trains and left about 7,000 people stuck at New Chitose. A or B: what would you do if it happened to you? 👇

🎯 Pick A or B, then see what JR Hokkaido itself suggests 👉 https://japanbystation.com/new-chitose-airport-to-sapporo

🅰️ Wait for the trains to restart.

🅱️ Head straight for the airport bus or a taxi.

Here's what we found. On disrupted days JR Hokkaido points travellers to the airport bus (about 70 to 90 minutes, about ¥1,500) or a taxi (about 60 minutes, from about ¥17,000), and warns that both get very crowded and slow down on bad roads.

✅ WHAT WE'D DO

Check JR Hokkaido's service status before you leave baggage claim. If trains are stopped, move early: the bus takes no reservations, so when it's full you wait for the next one.

🎫 Bought a ticket and the trip is off? Unused paper tickets are refunded in full, and a reserved u-seat booked online and not yet collected is cancelled automatically if its train is cancelled.

🏨 And when you book, choose a hotel close to the station or a bus stop, so a snow day never means dragging a suitcase across ice.

Snowy Sapporo is magical. A little planning keeps it that way from the moment you land.
